excerpt: Paano magtanim ng patani? Here is how traditional Filipino farmers usually plant patani (lima bean), step by step from getting the field ready to the harvest, with the day of each step and what to change for a higher yield.

blocks.title: This is the traditional way
blocks.text: This guide shows how traditional farmers usually plant patani. Use it as a starting point. For a higher yield, update it: plant certified seed or clean planting material, test your soil, and follow the right spacing and fertilizer.

How Filipino growers raise patani, the climbing lima bean grown along fences and on poles for its green seeds, a staple of pinakbet and ginataang gulay. It is seeded direct and bears for months.

Before you plant, get the field ready with our [land preparation guide for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation). Then choose your seed or planting material with the [patani varieties sold here](/crop-varieties/lima-bean). If the leaves turn pale later on, the [patani nutrient deficiency guide](/nutrient-deficiencies/lima-bean-nutrient-deficiency) helps you find what is missing.
When to plant patani
Planted at the start of the rains, around May to June, or from October to November. It is often grown along fences and backyard frames.
What you plant
Dry seed from fully mature pods. The big seed is planted direct, sometimes after a short soak.
Paano magtanim ng patani, step by step
Day 85 is about the first picking of green pods. The vine keeps bearing for months. The crop is ready about 85 days after sowing.
Before planting (Bago magtanim)

items.title: 14 days before sowing: Dig and add manure
items.text: Dig the plot or spots along the fence and mix in dried manure or compost.

blocks.text: Planting day (Pagtatanim)

items.title: Sowing day: Plant the seed
items.text: Plant 2 to 3 seeds a hill, with hills about a meter apart, and cover them with 3 to 5 cm of soil.

blocks.text: Care while it grows (Pag aalaga)

items.title: Day 14: Thin and put up poles
items.text: Leave the strongest one or two plants and set up poles, a frame or strings to the fence for the vines.

items.title: Day 21: Weed
items.text: Hoe out the weeds around the hills.

items.title: Day 30: Feed
items.text: Side dress complete fertilizer (14 14 14) or more manure around the plants.

items.title: Day 50: Watch for pests
items.text: Check the flowers and pods for pod borers and the leaves for aphids.

blocks.text: Harvest (Anihan)

items.title: Day 85: Pick the green pods
items.text: Pick the pods when they are plump and the seeds inside are full but still green, every few days.

items.title: Day 120: Keep seed pods
items.text: Leave some pods on the vine to dry for seed.

blocks.text: Spacing, water and fertilizer for patani
Spacing
Hills about a meter apart along poles, a frame or a fence.
Water
Rainfed, with hand watering in long dry spells.
Fertilizer

Dried manure or compost at planting, with a side dressing of complete fertilizer (14 14 14) or more manure after about a month. To read what a bag really gives, see our guide to [fertilizer for this crop](/blog/fertilizer-for-plants).
Care and harvest
Care while it grows
Support for the vines, weeding around the hills, and checking for pod borers and aphids.
When and how to harvest
Green pods are picked when the seeds are full but still green, every few days for months. Dry pods give next season's seed.
Common mistakes when planting patani

items: Planting the big seed too deep in wet soil, where it rots.
Letting the pods dry on the vine when green seeds are wanted.

blocks.text: How to get a higher yield of patani
The traditional way gets a crop, but small changes add up. These are the first things to change, one season at a time.

items: Plant fresh, whole seed into moist soil, not soggy soil.
Feed with compost and a side dressing and pick often.
Scout for pod borers at flowering.
